long_biography.plain_text:
Lawrence Sheldon Stroll entered fashion through a family business that held the Canadian children's-wear licence for Pierre Cardin. He expanded from that established platform, taking Ralph Lauren into Europe and forming Sportswear Holdings with Silas Chou in 1989. Their investments helped build Tommy Hilfiger and later Michael Kors, whose flotation became the central source of Stroll's fortune.

A longstanding interest in cars and racing then became his main business focus. Stroll led the consortium that acquired the Force India team, renamed Racing Point and later Aston Martin. He also led an investment in Aston Martin Lagonda and became its executive chairman in 2020. He now directs the road-car company's strategy while leading the business side of the associated Formula One operation.
